llm_analysis:
TSM’s 2023-Q4 prints a classic “volume recovery, profitability lag” setup. Revenue rebounded strongly QoQ (+13.6% USD), extending the re-acceleration from Q3 after a weak mid-2023, and working-capital metrics improved (inventory days -11 QoQ; AR days -4), consistent with healthier demand/supply balance and digestion of prior excess. However, the recovery is not yet translating into margin leverage: gross margin slipped to 53% (-1.3pp QoQ) and both gross/operating margins remain materially below the prior-cycle peak (FY23 GM -5.2pp YoY; FY23 OM -6.9pp YoY), with EPS down -17.5% YoY.

The most trade-relevant signal is the near-term growth air pocket implied by Q1’24 guidance (midpoint ~-6.2% QoQ). That tempers the Q4 upside surprise and suggests investors may need clearer evidence of sustained AI/HPC-driven mix improvement before re-rating margins. Macro is also a headwind for multiples: policy rates (5.33%) and long yields (4.44%) keep discount rates elevated, raising the bar for duration-heavy semiconductor valuations.

Bullish drivers: sequential revenue rebound, improving inventory/receivables efficiency, strong liquidity (US$55B cash/securities) supporting capex and resilience, and credible guidance framing. Bearish drivers: ongoing margin compression, negative YoY earnings power, and guidance implying deceleration; plus macro rates that can cap valuation expansion. With no peer data provided, relative positioning is neutral; overall stance is near-neutral with slightly elevated risk until margins stabilize and guidance turns up.

TSM’s 2023-Q4 prints a classic “volume recovery, profitability lag” setup. Revenue rebounded strongly QoQ (+13.6% USD), extending the re-acceleration from Q3 after a weak mid-2023, and working-capital metrics improved (inventory days -11 QoQ; AR days -4), consistent with healthier demand/supply balance and digestion of prior excess. However, the recovery is not yet translating into margin leverage: gross margin slipped to 53% (-1.3pp QoQ) and both gross/operating margins remain materially below the prior-cycle peak (FY23 GM -5.2pp YoY; FY23 OM -6.9pp YoY), with EPS down -17.5% YoY.

The most trade-relevant signal is the near-term growth air pocket implied by Q1’24 guidance (midpoint ~-6.2% QoQ). That tempers the Q4 upside surprise and suggests investors may need clearer evidence of sustained AI/HPC-driven mix improvement before re-rating margins. Macro is also a headwind for multiples: policy rates (5.33%) and long yields (4.44%) keep discount rates elevated, raising the bar for duration-heavy semiconductor valuations.

TSM’s 2024-Q1 print shows a familiar seasonal revenue dip (-5.3% QoQ NT$ / -3.8% QoQ US$), but the key historical signal is that the decline is far milder than the early-2023 reset and closer to mid-cycle softness—consistent with demand stabilization rather than renewed deterioration. More important for near-term trading, profitability held up: gross margin edged up to 53.1% and operating margin to 42%, suggesting mix/efficiency gains and cost discipline (opex 11.1% of revenue) are offsetting utilization pressure.

The forward setup is growth-led: Q2 revenue guidance implies a clear rebound (+6% QoQ at midpoint; +27.6% YoY), which is the strongest bullish catalyst in the dataset and likely to support positive revisions and positioning into the print. However, management is also flagging near-term margin friction: gross margin guide (51–53%) plus an explicit ~50bp earthquake headwind, with operating margin guided flat-to-down (40–42%). In a high-rate macro (Fed funds ~5.33%, 10Y ~4.16%), any disappointment on margins or capex intensity can be punished via multiple compression even if revenue recovers.

With no peer data provided, relative calls should be muted; the trade hinges on whether the Q2 rebound translates into sustained multi-quarter acceleration without sacrificing margins. Upside drivers: stronger-than-guided Q2 demand, improving utilization/mix, and operating leverage. Downside drivers: margin slippage from disruptions, slower-than-expected recovery after Q2, and valuation sensitivity to rates.

The forward setup is growth-led: Q2 revenue guidance implies a clear rebound (+6% QoQ at midpoint; +27.6% YoY), which is the strongest bullish catalyst in the dataset and likely to support positive revisions and positioning into the print. However, management is also flagging near-term margin friction: gross margin guide (51–53%) plus an explicit ~50bp earthquake headwind, with operating margin guided flat-to-down (40–42%). In a high-rate macro (Fed funds ~5.33%, 10Y ~4.16%), any disappointment on margins or capex intensity can be punished via multiple compression even if revenue recovers.

With no peer data provided, relative calls should be muted; the trade hinges on whether the Q2 rebound translates into sustained multi-quarter acceleration without sacrificing margins. Upside drivers: stronger-than-guided Q2 demand, improving utilization/mix, and operating leverage. Downside drivers: margin slippage from disruptions, slower-than-expected recovery after Q2, and valuation sensitivity to rates.

TSM’s 2024-Q2 print and Q3 guide signal a clear demand re-acceleration after a soft Q1, with revenue up +10.3% QoQ (USD) and Q3 midpoint guiding another +9.5% QoQ (+32% YoY). That sequential pattern—early-year dip then mid-year rebound—fits seasonality, but the magnitude plus strong forward growth suggests mix improvement (likely leading-edge/AI) rather than a purely calendar effect. Margins are not spiking, but they are steadily firming: gross margin +10bp QoQ to 53.2% and operating margin +0.5pp to 42.5%, with Q3 guidance implying modest further expansion. Cash generation remains a key support (TWD 378B CFO; ~$63B cash/securities), helping fund a large but controlled FY24 capex plan ($30–32B) without obvious balance-sheet stress.

Trading signals skew moderately constructive near-term: (1) sequential revenue acceleration plus upbeat Q3 guide, (2) stable-to-improving margin trajectory, and (3) strong operating leverage (opex 10.5% of revenue). Offsetting that, the macro backdrop is restrictive (policy rate ~5.33%, yields ~4.44%), which can pressure multiples and increase volatility in cyclical semis; additionally, elevated capex raises execution and utilization risk if end-demand broadens less than expected.

Upside drivers: sustained AI/HPC wafer demand, better pricing/mix at advanced nodes, and guide-driven estimate revisions. Downside drivers: macro-driven de-rating, customer digestion/seasonality reversal, and capex/geo-supply-chain execution risk. With no peer data provided, relative positioning remains neutral.

Margins are not spiking, but they are steadily firming: gross margin +10bp QoQ to 53.2% and operating margin +0.5pp to 42.5%, with Q3 guidance implying modest further expansion. Cash generation remains a key support (TWD 378B CFO; ~$63B cash/securities), helping fund a large but controlled FY24 capex plan ($30–32B) without obvious balance-sheet stress.

Trading signals skew moderately constructive near-term: (1) sequential revenue acceleration plus upbeat Q3 guide, (2) stable-to-improving margin trajectory, and (3) strong operating leverage (opex 10.5% of revenue). Offsetting that, the macro backdrop is restrictive (policy rate ~5.33%, yields ~4.44%), which can pressure multiples and increase volatility in cyclical semis; additionally, elevated capex raises execution and utilization risk if end-demand broadens less than expected.

Upside drivers: sustained AI/HPC wafer demand, better pricing/mix at advanced nodes, and guide-driven estimate revisions. Downside drivers: macro-driven de-rating, customer digestion/seasonality reversal, and capex/geo-supply-chain execution risk. With no peer data provided, relative positioning remains neutral.

However, profitability is no longer cleanly inflecting upward—gross margin slipped 0.2pp QoQ to 58.8% and operating margin fell 0.5pp to 48.5%, with Q2 margin guidance (GM 57–59%, OM 47–49%) implying stability-to-slight pressure rather than renewed expansion.

With no explicit peer data, relative positioning should be inferred cautiously: structurally high margins, strong ROE (32.7%), and a very large liquidity buffer (~US$81B cash/marketable securities) argue for resilience versus most semis, but the absence of peer confirmation keeps conviction moderate.

Macro is a mixed overlay: policy rates and yields remain restrictive (Fed funds ~4.33%, 10Y ~4.45%), which can cap multiple expansion even if fundamentals improve; unemployment is steady, reducing near-term recession risk.

Upside drivers: Q2 rebound execution, sustained AI/HPC demand translating into utilization and mix, and operating discipline. Downside drivers: margin compression from pricing/geo-manufacturing costs, capex intensity, and valuation sensitivity to rates if growth disappoints versus the strong guide.

Peer positioning is a blind spot here (no data), so conviction should lean on internal momentum: revenue and EPS trends are improving, but near-term profitability is guided lower. Upside drivers: stronger-than-guided Q3 revenue, better GM/OM realization vs guidance, and continued AI-driven mix. Downside drivers: deeper margin compression, FX/cost inflation, and valuation sensitivity to rates plus geopolitical/supply-chain risk.

TSM’s 2025-Q3 print reinforces an upcycle: revenue accelerated to $33.1B (+10.1% QoQ) while gross and operating margins expanded to 59.5% and 50.6%, respectively. The multi-quarter trajectory is notably constructive—operating margin has risen three straight quarters and EPS has stair-stepped higher, consistent with utilization/mix leverage as advanced nodes (7nm and below) remain a large 74% of wafer revenue and 3nm is already 23%. Management’s full-year outlook (mid-30s % USD growth) and narrowed, still-elevated 2025 CapEx range ($40–42B) signal confidence in sustained demand, likely tied to leading-edge compute/AI.

Near-term, Q4 guidance implies a typical seasonal pause (midpoint ~-1% QoQ) but with margins holding near Q3 (GM 59–61%, OM 49–51%). Importantly, Q3 margins beat prior guidance materially, suggesting conservative forecasting—often a supportive trading signal if demand remains intact.

Bullish drivers: continued margin resilience despite heavy investment, strong balance sheet (~$90B cash), and accelerating profitability momentum. Upside could come from faster 3nm/advanced-node mix shift, better-than-guided Q4, or easing rates improving semiconductor multiples.

Bearish/risk drivers: macro is not “easy” (policy rate and yields ~4.3%), which can cap valuation expansion; very high CapEx raises execution and cycle-risk if demand normalizes; and with no peer data here, relative positioning vs other foundries/IDMs is uncertain. Net: positive fundamentals with a near-term growth pause; sentiment modestly bullish but not extreme given macro and capex/cycle risk.

The multi-quarter trajectory is notably constructive—operating margin has risen three straight quarters and EPS has stair-stepped higher, consistent with utilization/mix leverage as advanced nodes (7nm and below) remain a large 74% of wafer revenue and 3nm is already 23%. Net: positive fundamentals with a near-term growth pause; sentiment modestly bullish but not extreme given macro and capex/cycle risk.

TSM exits 2025 with strong fundamental quality and improving near-term setup, but the trading signal is not one-way because sequential growth is moderating even as margins surge. Q4 revenue rose +1.9% QoQ in USD (+5.7% in NT$, highlighting FX tailwind), following a much larger Q2→Q3 step-up; this suggests demand remains robust but the pace of sequential acceleration has cooled. The more important positive signal is profitability: gross margin jumped to 62.3% (+2.8pp QoQ) and operating margin to 54% (+3.4pp QoQ), extending a multi-quarter inflection and implying favorable mix/leading-node utilization and operating leverage. Guidance adds confirmation: Q1’26 midpoint implies +4% QoQ and +38% YoY, and management has recently guided conservatively (Q4 GM beat the 59–61% range).

Balance sheet and cash generation remain a cushion (TWD 3.1T cash; FY FCF ~TWD 1T), while the 2026 capex budget (USD 52–56B) is an upside driver if it translates into sustained technology leadership and capacity for AI/HPC demand. The same capex is also the key downside driver: if macro tightness (policy rate ~3.9%, yields ~4.1%) or end-demand normalizes, elevated spend could pressure future free cash flow and raise cycle risk. With no peer data provided, relative positioning is harder to handicap; trading should key off (1) whether Q1’26 growth prints at/above midpoint and (2) whether margins hold near 60%+ as capex ramps.
